LLDAP_PORT.description: LLDAP Web UI port — bound to the host loopback (127.0.0.1) since template v3, so it is only reachable on the box itself or via the Authelia-gated ldap.<domain> proxy host (#2380).

LLDAP_LDAP_PORT.description: LDAP protocol port. Still bound to every host interface — it cannot be loopback-bound, because isolated pods (radicale, media/Jellyfin LDAP-Auth) reach it via host.containers.internal, which rootless podman/pasta maps to the host's LAN address rather than loopback. LAN devices are instead refused at the HOST firewall via the blockLanAccess flag below (#2388): ServiceBay installs an nftables rule that drops connections arriving on a physical interface while leaving loopback and the pasta-proxied pod path (which lands on lo) untouched.

LLDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD.description: LLDAP admin password — auto-generated. Saved to Settings → Integrations → LLDAP after install so you can retrieve it for first login (user: admin).

LLDAP_JWT_SECRET.description: JWT secret for LLDAP session tokens

LLDAP_SUBDOMAIN.description: Subdomain for LLDAP Web UI. Gated by Authelia forward-auth (admin group, two-factor per Authelia's access_control rules). Without the forward-auth block, the LLDAP UI is reachable at the nginx layer by any logged-in family user — the admin-only Authelia rule never fires because nginx never makes the auth_request subrequest (#878). That case is about a misconfigured proxy; the separate direct-on-LAN bypass (a LAN host hitting <lan-ip>:LLDAP_PORT and never touching nginx at all) is closed in template v3 by binding LLDAP's HTTP server to 127.0.0.1 plus the loopbackOnly flag below (#2380). The raw LDAP port had the same direct-on-LAN shape; it cannot be loopback-bound, so it is closed one layer down instead — see LLDAP_LDAP_PORT's blockLanAccess flag (#2388).

AUTHELIA_JWT_SECRET.description: JWT secret for Authelia identity verification

AUTHELIA_OIDC_HMAC_SECRET.description: HMAC secret for OIDC token signing

AUTHELIA_OIDC_RSA_PRIVATE_KEY.description: RSA private key (PEM) for OIDC token signing — Authelia 4.39+ requires a real key, no longer auto-generates one. Server-generated 2048-bit at install time.

SERVICEBAY_OIDC_SECRET.description: OIDC client secret for the `servicebay` client — the one Authelia checks when you press "Login with Authelia" on ServiceBay's own admin panel. Auto-generated per box (template v4, #2417); before that the client shipped one hardcoded literal identical on every install. This variable is the SINGLE source of truth: it is rendered into Authelia's `configuration.yml` clients[] block, and after that file lands ServiceBay copies the value it finds on disk into its own `config.oidc.clientSecret`. Both sides must hold the same value or the SSO button fails with `invalid_client` — the local admin username/password login on the same page is the break-glass path if they ever drift.

AUTHELIA_STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY.description: Encryption key for Authelia SQLite storage (min 20 chars)

LLDAP_HOST.description: LLDAP host — always localhost when bundled with Authelia in the auth pod.

LLDAP_FORCE_LDAP_USER_PASS_RESET.description: Dynamic self-healing flag for resetting admin password during install-time drift
